title: From coding to Knowledge work agents — Karan Vaidya, Composio
talk_summary: Karan Vaidya argues coding agents succeeded because of infrastructure around code (centralized source of truth, history, verification, governance, reversibility), not just better models, and proposes six primitives to bring that substrate to knowledge work. The talk is mostly a Composio product pitch, but the governance, sandboxing, and verification mechanisms are concrete and copyable.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic capability walls outside the prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Enforce what an agent can reach via access control that lives outside the agent's context, so it cannot be argued with, forgotten, or compacted away; layer natural-language policies on top for behavior within that reach.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The boundary lives outside these agents. It can't be argued with by the agent or forgotten or compacted.

takeaways.what_they_do: For actions with no undo, run them first against mocked tools in a sandbox, surface the diff/plan for review, then execute for real.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of the blast radius hitting the real world, it will hit a sandbox, and then I can review it before the agent does the real thing.

takeaways.technique: Pre-action style/quality check against past accepted work
takeaways.what_they_do: Before an agent sends anything, compare the draft against a corpus of previously approved outputs to check it matches house style and quality bar.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before the agent senses anything, it checks the draft emails that I've sent before. If it matches my style

takeaways.technique: Centralized action log as agent memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Log every agent action across tools in one place so agents can look back at how similar tasks succeeded/failed instead of starting blank, and humans can audit what actually happened.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every single like action that agent takes can be logged across every other app. Whatever it touched, whatever it skipped, what worked, what didn't.

takeaways.technique: Tiered governance gates by blast radius
takeaways.what_they_do: Multiple gates of varying strictness depending on blast radius: agents free on their own branch, human review before main, code owners on critical files, preview-only deploys.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The governance is not a single gate, but multiple of them, and each varying its sizes depending on the blast radius it exposes.

takeaways.technique: Distill logged runs into reusable skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Mine the action log for patterns of what worked and failed, distilling them into skills/playbooks the agent can query instead of re-deriving process each time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you log enough of what every agent is doing, you start to see patterns... you start to form skills
